Update an Individual SEM Graph Node

Source: R/plot-update_graph.R
update_graph_node.Rd

update_graph_node() provides a convenient way to modify a single node without manually editing the graph's node data frame.

The function updates the selected node and recalculates its bounding box while preserving the remaining graph structure.

Usage

update_graph_node(x, name, ..., group = NULL, level = NULL)

Arguments

x

An object of class sem_graph.

name

Character string identifying the node to update.

...

Named node properties to modify. These may include x, y, width, height, shape, label, or supported plotting aesthetics such as colour, fill, alpha, linetype, and linewidth.

group

Optional group identifier, used to distinguish nodes with the same name in grouped graphs.

level

Optional level identifier, used to distinguish nodes with the same name across levels.

Value

An updated object of class sem_graph.

Details

Modify the position, dimensions, label, shape, or aesthetics of an individual node in an existing SEM graph.

Node positions are specified in the graph's existing coordinate system and are not rescaled.

Individual width and height values override the global dimensions specified when the graph was constructed.

When node dimensions or shape are modified, the node's bounding box is updated automatically.

If multiple nodes share the same name, group or level can be used to identify the intended node.

Edge endpoints, connection sides, curvature, and variance positions are not automatically recalculated.

See also

update_graph(), prepare_graph()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
g <- prepare_graph(
  edges = edges,
  nodes = nodes,
  layout = layout
)

# Move a node
g <- update_graph_node(
  g,
  name = "visual",
  x = 5,
  y = 4
)

# Change its dimensions and appearance
g <- update_graph_node(
  g,
  name = "visual",
  width = 1.8,
  height = 1.2,
  fill = "lightblue",
  colour = "black"
)

plot(g)
} # }
